# HANDBOOK

<!-- generated by `make handbook` from the command registry — edit the
     eval.Register declarations beside each builtin, not this file -->

Command mode's vocabulary: every word here is safe to type at the prompt —
no name that shadows a system binary appears (`ls`, `grep`, `cat`, ... always
mean the real programs; the Scheme spellings stay reachable with parens).
Every command answers `-h`/`--help` with its short usage; `help` opens the
man-formatted manual at the prompt — `help <command>` is that command's man
page, `help --list | grep rank` filters the pages as rows. `(builtins)` lists
every callable including the Scheme library.

## Commands

Stage means the word is also valid after a `|`, the piped value threading
in as the last argument.

| command | stage | description |
|---|---|---|
| add-path |  | idempotently prepend directories to PATH |
| agent | ✓ | run a sub-agent chat turn — the rest of the line is the instruction |
| aliases |  | command-mode aliases as rows |
| bm25 | ✓ | rank items by BM25 keyword relevance to a query |
| builtins |  | every registered callable as rows |
| chunk | ✓ | split text into chunks for embedding |
| classify | ✓ | label each item via the LLM — history \| take 50 \| classify "bug-fix or feature?" \| count-by label |
| clear |  | clear the screen and start a fresh session |
| compact |  | summarize older turns to shrink the chat context |
| configure |  | interactive setup: provider, model, thinking, claude code hooks |
| count-by | ✓ | count rows per column value — history \| count-by project |
| create-graph |  | create a new named graph |
| create-project |  | create a bare-repo project hub under the project root and cd in |
| create-tree |  | add a branch worktree to the current project |
| delete-edge |  | delete edges by id |
| delete-graph |  | delete a named graph and its contents (asks y/N) |
| delete-node |  | delete nodes by id (their edges cascade) |
| delete-task |  | delete tasks by id — permanent; task -c closes instead |
| delete-tree |  | remove a project worktree |
| dir |  | list a directory as rows, ls under a non-shadowing name |
| edges |  | list a graph's edges as id/source/target/type rows |
| embed |  | a text's embedding vector as a list of numbers |
| fetch |  | fetch an http(s) url, body as a line stream |
| fg |  | resume the most recently stopped job in the foreground (user-only) |
| from-csv | ✓ | parse CSV into rows — from-csv data.csv --sep ";" |
| graph |  | a named graph's stats — node/edge counts and metadata |
| graphs |  | list graphs as rows with node/edge counts |
| group-by | ✓ | group rows by a column into a {value: rows} dictionary — history \| group-by project \| keys |
| help |  | the rf manual: an overview page, topic pages, a man page per command |
| history |  | search command history |
| hybrid | ✓ | rank items by fused keyword+semantic relevance |
| inspect |  | show a definition's source, reconstructed from the live closure |
| job |  | start a background command, returning a handle — -s polls, -w joins, -o peeks at output, -k stops; --in delays it, --every reruns it |
| jobs |  | stopped, background, and job-builtin children as rows |
| llm | ✓ | one plain LLM completion — the piped value threads in as context |
| llm-map | ✓ | map an LLM instruction over items, replies as a new llm column — history \| take 20 \| llm-map "one-line summary" |
| messages |  | search chat messages across rf and Claude Code sessions |
| neighbors |  | a node's neighboring nodes as rows with a direction column |
| nodes |  | list a graph's nodes as rows; a query full-text searches them ranked |
| parse-json | ✓ | parse JSON (a file, stream, or lines) into Scheme values — fetch url \| parse-json |
| paths |  | the PATH entries as {:path} rows |
| persist |  | promote a definition to the prelude via a sub-agent |
| pick | ✓ | keep only the named columns — ls \| pick name size |
| project |  | cd into a project's worktree directory |
| projects |  | list registered projects as rows |
| recall |  | search remembered notes |
| register-project |  | register a directory (cwd by default) as a project |
| remember |  | save a note to the default graph |
| remove-path |  | remove directories from PATH |
| rename-session |  | rename this console session (needs rf console) |
| rerank | ✓ | reorder retrieved rows by listwise LLM relevance judgment — bm25 "query" corpus -n 100 \| rerank "query" |
| resume |  | pick a past session and continue it |
| session |  | open a console session running COMMAND — now, or scheduled with --in/--at/--every; named by --name or a slug of the command (needs rf console) |
| sessions |  | list the console's sessions as rows — live ones, then scheduled ones with their next run (needs rf console) |
| similar | ✓ | rank items by semantic similarity to a query |
| sort-by | ✓ | sort rows by a column, or items by themselves — ls \| sort-by size -r |
| task |  | file a task for the current project |
| tasks |  | list the current project's open tasks as rows |
| top-incoming |  | nodes ranked by incoming edge count, as rows with a count column |
| top-outgoing |  | nodes ranked by outgoing edge count, as rows with a count column |
| tree |  | cd into a project worktree, creating it if missing |
| trees |  | list the current project's worktrees as rows |
| unalias |  | remove a command-mode alias |
| unregister-project |  | remove a project from the registry |
| usage |  | session token totals, cost, and context size |
| where | ✓ | filter rows by field comparisons (= != -gt -lt -ge -le, chained with and/or) or a predicate — dir \| where type = file and size -gt 100MB |

## Pipeline-only stages

Valid after a `|` but not as a line's first word.

| stage | description |
|---|---|
| append-file | append a value to a file — the pipeline's >> redirection |
| get | index into a collection — (get key coll) |
| json | serialize a value as JSON lines |
| keys | a dictionary's keys |
| length | the number of elements |
| string-downcase | lowercase a string (full Unicode case mapping) |
| string-upcase | uppercase a string (full Unicode case mapping) |
| table | render rows as an aligned table string |
| take | the first n elements of a stream or list |
| text | serialize a value as plain text lines — rows become TSV |
| write-file | write a value to a file — the pipeline's > redirection |

## Scheme library

The rest of `(builtins)` — every registered function with no command-mode
presence, callable with parens in any mode; `help <name>` at the prompt.

| function | description |
|---|---|
| * | the product of its arguments |
| + | the sum of its arguments |
| - | subtract successive arguments; (- x) negates |
| / | division across arguments; exact when it divides evenly; (/ x) is the reciprocal |
| < | numeric less-than across arguments |
| <= | numeric less-or-equal across arguments |
| = | numeric equality; use equal? for other values |
| > | numeric greater-than across arguments |
| >= | numeric greater-or-equal across arguments |
| abs | the absolute value of a number |
| acos | arccosine, in radians |
| add-edge | add an edge from a dictionary with source/target node ids |
| add-node | add a node from a dictionary, returning its id (default graph) |
| alias | define a command-mode alias — (alias ll "ls -la") |
| and | short-circuit: false at the first falsy argument, else the last value; (and) is true |
| append | concatenate lists; the last argument may be any tail value |
| apply | call fn with a list as its trailing arguments: (apply fn lst) |
| asin | arcsine, in radians |
| assert | error unless a condition holds: (assert cond [message]) |
| assoc | the first alist entry whose key matches, else false: (assoc obj alist [compare]) |
| assq | the first alist entry whose key is eq?, else false |
| assv | the first alist entry whose key is eqv?, else false |
| atan | arctangent: (atan y) or (atan y x) |
| basename | the file part of a path |
| begin | evaluate expressions in order, returning the last |
| binary-port? | port direction/kind predicate |
| boolean=? | whether all booleans are the same |
| boolean? | true when the value is a boolean |
| bytevector | a fresh bytevector of its byte arguments |
| bytevector-append | concatenate bytevectors into a fresh bytevector |
| bytevector-copy | a fresh copy of a bytevector: (bytevector-copy bv [start [end]]) |
| bytevector-copy! | copy a range between bytevectors in place: (bytevector-copy! to at from [start [end]]) |
| bytevector-length | the number of bytes in a bytevector |
| bytevector-u8-ref | the byte at an index: (bytevector-u8-ref bv k) |
| bytevector-u8-set! | replace the byte at an index in place |
| bytevector? | true when the value is a bytevector |
| caaaar | the car of the car of the car of the car of a list |
| caaadr | the car of the car of the car of the cdr of a list |

| string-for-each | call a procedure on each character for its effects: (string-for-each proc string...) |
| string-join | join a list of strings with a separator |
| string-length | the number of characters in a string |
| string-map | map a procedure over strings' characters: (string-map proc string...) |
| string-prefix? | whether a string starts with a prefix |
| string-ref | the character at an index: (string-ref s k) |
| string-replace | replace every occurrence of a substring |
| string-set! | replace the character at an index in place |
| string-split | split a string on a separator into a list of strings |
| string-suffix? | whether a string ends with a suffix |
| string-trim | strip whitespace (or a cutset's characters) from both ends |
| string<=? | lexicographic string less-or-equal across arguments |
| string<? | lexicographic string less-than across arguments |
| string=? | whether strings are equal |
| string>=? | lexicographic string greater-or-equal across arguments |
| string>? | lexicographic string greater-than across arguments |
| string? | true when the value is a string |
| substring | a slice of a string: (substring s start [end]) |
| symbol->string | a symbol's name as a string |
| symbol=? | whether all symbols are the same |
| symbol? | true when the value is a symbol |
| syntax-error | signal a syntax error: (syntax-error "message" form...) |
| syntax-rules | a macro transformer: (syntax-rules (literal...) (pattern template)...) |
| tan | tangent of an angle in radians |
| textual-port? | port direction/kind predicate |
| truncate | drop a number's fractional part, toward zero |
| truncate-quotient | truncated integer division (quotient) |
| truncate-remainder | truncated remainder (remainder) |
| truncate/ | truncated quotient and remainder as two values |
| u8-ready? | true when a byte is ready on a binary input port |
| unless | evaluate body forms if a test is false |
| unquote | evaluate a hole inside a quasiquote template |
| unquote-splicing | splice a list into a quasiquote template |
| update-node | replace a node's properties from a dictionary with an id key |
| utf8->string | decode a bytevector's UTF-8 as a string: (utf8->string bv [start [end]]) |
| values | return multiple values to a call-with-values consumer |
| vector | a fresh vector of its arguments |
| vector->list | a vector's elements as a fresh list: (vector->list vec [start [end]]) |
| vector->string | a vector of characters as a string: (vector->string vec [start [end]]) |
| vector-append | concatenate vectors into a fresh vector |
| vector-copy | a fresh copy of a vector: (vector-copy vec [start [end]]) |
| vector-copy! | copy a range between vectors in place: (vector-copy! to at from [start [end]]) |
| vector-fill! | fill a vector range in place: (vector-fill! vec fill [start [end]]) |
| vector-for-each | call a function elementwise over vectors for effect: (vector-for-each fn vec...) |
| vector-length | the number of elements in a vector |
| vector-map | apply a function elementwise over vectors: (vector-map fn vec...) |
| vector-ref | the element at an index: (vector-ref vec k) |
| vector-set! | replace the element at an index in place |
| vector? | true when the value is a vector |
| wc | line, word and byte counts as a row |
| when | evaluate body forms if a test is true |
| which | locate a command on PATH |
| with-approval | run body forms behind one approval prompt instead of per-operation gates |
| with-exception-handler | install an exception handler for a thunk's dynamic extent |
| with-graph | evaluate body forms with the named graph as the target |
| with-input-from-file | run a thunk with current-input-port reading a file |
| with-output-to-file | run a thunk with current-output-port writing a file |
| write | write a value in reader syntax (cycles as datum labels): (write obj [port]) |
| write-bytevector | write a bytevector (or its [start,end) range) to a binary output port |
| write-char | write one character to a textual output port |
| write-shared | write with labels for all shared structure |
| write-simple | write without shared-structure labels |
| write-string | write a string (or its [start,end) range) to a textual output port |
| write-u8 | write one byte to a binary output port |
| zero? | whether a number is zero |

### job

```
job — start a background command, returning a handle — -s polls, -w joins, -o peeks at output, -k stops; --in delays it, --every reruns it

usage:  job "command" [flags]
scheme: (job "command" [{:in SPAN :every SPAN :status JOB :wait JOB :output JOB :kill JOB :stderr #t :timeout SECONDS}])

      --in SPAN          start after SPAN (30s, 10m, 4h, 1d, 1w)
      --every SPAN       rerun every SPAN (hour, day, week, or a span) until killed; lives with this shell
  -s, --status JOB       poll job JOB: {:job :command :state :running [:exit]}
  -w, --wait JOB         join job JOB and return {:stdout :stderr :exit} (a recurring job's next finished run)
  -o, --output JOB       job JOB's captured output so far as lines, without blocking — job -o 3 | tail -20
  -k, --kill JOB         stop job JOB (interrupt, then kill) and cancel its schedule
      --stderr           with --output: the stderr buffer instead of stdout
  -t, --timeout SECONDS  with --wait: give up after SECONDS (the job keeps running)
  -h, --help             this help
```

scheme: (session [command] [{:name NAME :dir PATH :in SPAN :at TIME :every SPAN :cancel #t}])

  -d, --dir PATH    working directory (default: this shell's cwd)

      --every SPAN  reopen every SPAN (hour, day, week, or a span); a run still up gets a numbered name (review-2)
      --cancel      drop the schedule of this name
